name: New Mexico
covers_nil_agents: Yes. An agency contract includes endorsement contracts (NMSA 61-14F-2). Schools can't stop athletes from hiring NIL representation (NMSA 21-31-4).
summary: Register with the Secretary of State. $250, good for 2 years.

steps.text: Fill out the New/Renewal Athlete Agent Application

steps.detail: $200 if you use another state's registration.

steps.text: Register with each school's compliance office, if it asks
steps.detail: Most schools have their own agent sign-up.

steps.text: Use a written contract with all required items
steps.detail: Your pay and how it's figured, anyone else being paid, expenses, services, length and date signed.

steps.text: Put the warning to the student athlete in bold capital letters near their signature
steps.detail: Use the exact words the law gives.

steps.text: Tell the athlete before they sign that signing may cost them eligibility
Give the athlete a copy when they sign
Tell the athletic director in writing within 72 hours of signing
steps.detail: Or before the athlete's next game, whichever comes first. The athlete may cancel within 14 days.

steps.text: Date the contract the day it's signed
steps.detail: State law and federal law (SPARTA) both ban pre-dating or post-dating it.
Names and addresses of your athletes, every contract and what you spent to recruit each one. The Secretary of State can inspect them.

steps.text: Never give an athlete anything of value before they sign, or make false promises
steps.detail: Also never give anything to anyone else to get an athlete to sign. Breaking these rules is a misdemeanor.
Your registration lasts 2 years. It's $200 if you renew using another state's renewal.

watch_list.item: Federal Protect College Sports Act of 2026 (S.4668)
watch_list.status: Passed the Senate on Sept 28, 2026. The House is out until Nov 9 and leaders say it won't pass as-is. It dies if not enacted by Jan 3, 2027.
watch_list.impact: It would require every NIL agent to register in a state, cap agent fees at 5% of an endorsement deal and limit contracts to the athlete's eligibility.

review_notes: The statute was read from Justia (2025 edition for 61-14F-10, 2021 edition for 61-14F-11 and 61-14F-14) and the 2009 act on the Secretary of State's site. History notes show no changes since 2009. Confirm the current text on nmonesource.com.
The Secretary of State's pages don't say how to send the application or give a phone number for athlete agents. Ask the Secretary of State (325 Don Gaspar, Suite 300, Santa Fe) how to file.
An earlier version said military members and veterans may get a fee waiver. That was not found in the athlete agent law or fee page. Confirm with the Secretary of State before telling agents.
contract_warning: Warning to student athlete. If you sign this contract: (1) you may lose your eligibility to compete as a student athlete in your sport; (2) if you have an athletic director, within seventy-two hours after entering into this contract, both you and your athlete agent must notify your athletic director; and (3) you may cancel this contract within fourteen days after signing it. Cancellation of this contract may not reinstate your eligibility.
